about: The hand-kept register of every outside body this site takes data from or cites: who they are (bodies only), what they publish, what we take, the licence as published. tools/source-index.mjs adds the counts and writes sources.json and index.md from it. A body's own folder (sources/<id>/) appears as it is built; MeteoAlarm is first. `entity` is the id of the same body in entities/ (incident.entities@), where one exists. `also` lists the plain names a body is written by, for the linker.

sources.name: MeteoAlarm
sources.kind: EUMETNET's system that carries Europe's national weather warnings
sources.publishes: each national service's warnings as CAP messages: JSON and Atom feeds per country (open); an EDR API with the archive, MQTT, metadata (token or MeteoGate key)
sources.we_take: the time IPMA issued each warning, and which message it replaced

licence.summary: CC BY 4.0 equivalent, with additional requirements (name the national service, keep the time of issue, link www.meteoalarm.org, publish the disclaimer; real time if operational)

sources.reads: about hourly by tools/source-meteoalarm.mjs; about every 5 to 30 minutes by the meteorologist's refresh.py

sources.name: IPMA (Instituto Português do Mar e da Atmosfera)
sources.kind: Portugal's national meteorological service: it issues the warnings
sources.publishes: warnings, forecasts, station observations, communiqués, sea state (open data as JSON; RSS)
sources.we_take: the warnings in force, the hour-by-hour forecast for Lisbon, the stations' observations, the communiqués

licence.note: see sources/ipma/ (incident.ipma@'s section). The earlier check (research/weather-sites/meteoalarm-check.json) records that IPMA asks for the source to be named.

sources.reads: every 5 to 30 minutes (refresh.py); hourly by incident.ipma@
also: Instituto Português do Mar e da Atmosfera
